title: Night Shift
intro: Everybody rolls their quads. This one goes where tennis actually lands. Your feet. The deep calf that helps you brake. The inside of the thigh from wide balls and the outside from pushing off. The backs of your thighs from all the stopping. Then your mid back and chest from serving and overheads, and three minutes of slow breathing to finish. You need a roller and a ball, and a tennis ball is fine. Slow is the whole technique. When you find a sore spot, stop on it and take three breaths. Don't saw back and forth. Aim for firm pressure. If it's sharp, or you get pins and needles, back off.

Rolling helps you feel better and move a bit easier for a while, and that's genuinely it. It doesn't clear anything out of your muscles and it doesn't break anything up. So do it because the day is over and you want to feel human. Never roll your lower back, the front or side of your neck, the back of your knee, the inside of your elbow, your armpit or right into the groin crease. And nothing that's swollen, hot, bruised or freshly hurt. If something grabbed during play and it's still sore now, leave that spot alone and get it looked at. If one calf is swollen, warm or tender and you didn't strain it playing, don't roll it and see a doctor the same day.

good: Sit on a chair and roll a tennis ball slowly under your foot, from the heel to the ball
Feel the ball pressing into the sole of your foot, firm but not sharp
bad: Standing up and putting your full weight on the ball

exercises.name: Soleus Roll
exercises.note: If your calf is still sore from playing, skip this one.

good: Rest one calf on the roller with the knee bent and roll from the ankle up to below the knee
Feel the deep calf muscle under the big one
bad: Rolling up into the back of the knee

exercises.name: Adductor Roll
exercises.note: If a groin is still sore from playing, skip this one.

good: Lie face down with one leg out to the side and the roller under your inner thigh
Feel a dull, heavy pressure that eases when you breathe out
bad: Rolling right up into the groin crease

good: Lie on your side with the roller under your outer thigh and roll from just below the hip bone to just above the knee, holding some of your weight on your arms
Feel the outer thigh soften as the leg settles onto the roller
bad: Rolling over the side of the knee

good: Sit with the roller under one thigh and the other foot on the floor, then roll from just below the sit bone to a hand's width above the back of the knee
Feel the back of your thigh soften as your weight sinks into the roller
bad: Rolling into the back of the knee

good: Lie back over the roller under your shoulder blades and cradle your head in your hands
Feel your upper back opening over the roller
bad: Letting your neck or lower back do the bending

good: Stand facing a wall with the ball between the wall and one side of your chest muscle, and roll slowly, staying off the collarbone and breastbone
Feel firm pressure across the chest, not the shoulder joint

exercises.name: Extended Exhale Breathing
exercises.note: If you feel dizzy or tingly, go back to normal breathing.

good: Lie on your back with one hand on your belly and let each breath out slowly empty it
Feel that hand rise and fall while your chest stays quiet
